relevance_note: Case report of one patient with a GFAP variant: "Sanger sequencing analysis of GFAP disclosed a novel heterozygous c.619-1G>A mutation"; two previously published GFAP-variant patients are also described individually in the Discussion.
method_note: Hand extraction, no tables in the paper; JSON assembled by a short script from hand-written values. In scope: the case-report patient ('patient'); 'ref 3 patient' (heterozygous c.619-3C>G with exon 4 skipping, ref 3) and 'ref 7 patient' (p.Glu207Val, dysphagia and dysarthria at age 52, ref 7), each given individual-level facts. Left out: patients with p.Glu207Gln (ref 5) and p.Glu207Lys (ref 6), described only as a group ('Patients with p.Glu207Gln and p.Glu207Lys were juvenile onset') with no stated number of people. Features in the title of reference 7 (ataxia, palatal tremor) were not used, as they are only a cited article title. Age 76 is the age at presentation ('A 76-year-old man ... presented with progressive diplopia'), recorded as onset; the paper calls the disease 'very-late-onset' but gives no separate onset age, diagnosis age or age at death (died 6 months after diagnosis). The diplopia, ptosis and cranial nerve III/IV/VI palsies coincide with a left orbital schwannoma that the authors consider 'not to be related to ALXDRD'; they are recorded as observed features of the person (checklist eye movement item observed) without attribution. 'no other neurologic abnormalities were observed' is a whole-examination statement and was not used to exclude any checklist item. 'mild periventricular hyperintensity lesion' recorded as cerebral white matter abnormality; not taken as a periventricular rim. Inconsistency: the Figure title prints 'c.619 G>A' while text and legend print 'c.619-1G>A'; the legend also writes 'p. Glu207del' with a space. The protein consequence p.Glu207del is from the authors' brain RNA analysis (r.619_621del), not a prediction. No transcript printed. Parental testing not reported; family history of neurologic disease negative.

span: analysis of RNA from the autopsied brain tissue of the present patient showed deletion of GAG (r.619_621del)
The number of wild-type and mutant clones was 34 and 20, respectively.

These findings suggested that c.619-1G>A caused activation of the cryptic splice acceptor site in the second and third nucleotides from the 5′ end of exon 4 (Figure D), in approximately 37% (20/54) of the transcripts.
